newsitem.title: GERMANY: Atmosphere electric as Telekom lists in Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: Atmosphere electric as Telekom lists in Frankfurt.

text.p: A single official's shout of "33.20" opened the floodgate to frantic order activity on the Frankfurt bourse on Monday as dealers scrambled to book the first trades in Germany's newly-listed Telekom share.

Over 100 dealers waved their order-books at the official brokers handling trade in the stock, which started trade at 33.20 marks at 1130 GMT. The shares in the majority state-owned had been issued on Sunday at a price of 28.50 marks.

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Telekom chief executive Ron Sommer stood in the midst of the trading floor activity grinning as they watched the start of a flotation which has finally grabbed the imagination of the traditionally conservative small German investor.
The chief executives of Germany's top banks, Deutsche Bank's Hilmar Kopper and Dresdner Bank's Juergen Sarrazin, looked down on the scene from a staircase at the side of the bourse floor.
"You hardly ever see floor trade this busy," a bourse spokesman said.
Reflecting the level of interest in the issue, about 23.6 million Telekom shares were traded at the official opening price. The volume jumped to 26.09 million after 20 minutes of trading.
